name: Macau International Airport
before:
Macau's airport, at the eastern end of Taipa island and partly on the water beside it. It opened on 9 November 1995, while Macau was still under Portuguese administration.

The border arrangement is what makes it unusually useful. A "two customs, one checkpoint" service lets passengers take a shuttle bus straight from the airport to the New Macau Ferry Terminal or the Taipa Ferry Terminal without clearing Macau immigration at all, which matters for anyone routing on to Hong Kong or the mainland. The same service works at the Hengqin border.

It has long been a transfer point between mainland China and Taiwan, and a hub for mainland and Southeast Asian routes.

Capacity is the pressure point. The terminal was designed for 6 million passengers a year and handled 7,165,803 in 2017. The airport's stated design capacity is 10 million a year, or up to 2,300 passengers an hour.

The Macau Light Rail Transit Taipa Line has a station at the airport, and cross-border coaches run to Guangzhou, Dongguan, Gongbei and Hengqin.
after:
Macau's airport, at the eastern end of Taipa island. It opened in November 1995.

Connections are what make it useful. The airport's Express Link bus takes departing passengers from the Outer Harbour and Taipa ferry terminals straight into its restricted area. It also runs from the airport's check-in centre at the Macau port of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge, which mainly serves tour groups and passengers with bookings.

The terminal was first built for six million passengers a year. Extensions on its north and south sides, in use from 2018 and 2022, lifted capacity to 10 million a year, according to the aviation authority. In 2025 the airport counted about 7.5 million passengers.

The Macau Light Rail Transit has a station at the airport, and cross-border coaches run to Guangzhou, Dongguan, Gongbei and Hengqin.
